title: Why Are Tarot Readers Asking Robots for Advice?
summary: Have you ever asked Siri or Alexa for advice? You're not alone! Lots of people now use AI chatbots for emotional support. But here's a twist: some tarot card readers are asking AI to help them understand their readings. Tarot is a deck of 78 cards with special symbols. People use them to think about big questions, like "Should I quit my job?" or "What's going on in the world?" Usually, the reader looks at the cards and thinks about their own life to find meaning. But a new study from April 2026 found that some readers now let AI do the thinking. The researchers talked to 12 tarot readers. They found that readers liked how AI could quickly explain tricky card combinations. For example, if you pull the Fool card (which means a leap into the unknown) and the Ten of Wands (which means you're carrying too much), AI might give a clear answer. But the readers also felt weird about it. AI doesn't know your personal story, so its advice might not fit your real life. Tarot is supposed to be about your own feelings and choices, not a robot's guess. Still, almost 1 in 3 Americans try tarot or astrology each year, and now AI is part of that world too. It's a strange mix of old magic and new tech!
why_it_matters: It shows that even old traditions like tarot are mixing with new technology, just like how you might use apps to explore your own hobbies.

background_read: Tarot cards were first made in Europe over 500 years ago, originally for playing games, not telling the future.
Today, many people use tarot to reflect on their own feelings, while others just enjoy the beautiful art.
AI helpers like Siri and Alexa have become so common that people even ask them for advice about their day.
Article_Structure: WHO: Tarot card readers, researchers, and AI chatbots
WHAT: Tarot readers using AI to explain card meanings, even though AI doesn't know personal stories
WHERE: In the United States, where many people try tarot or astrology
WHY: AI gives quick answers to tricky card combinations, but some readers feel it misses the human touch

perspectives.description: Some tarot readers like that AI can quickly make sense of confusing card combinations, giving them a faster way to get a clear answer.
Other readers worry that relying on AI takes away the personal part of tarot, because a robot cannot know your life story and what you really need.
Researchers find it interesting to see how people blend old spiritual practices with modern technology, and they want to understand what this mixing means for the future.
